adrs.name: Double-booking behavior
adrs.description: Northgate overbooks deliberately in harvest season and reallocates by seniority.
adrs.question: Should a second hold on a booked machine be blocked, warned, or pooled?
adrs.decision: Soft warning with a conflict queue.
adrs.rationale: Preserves the overbooking the operation depends on, makes clashes visible, and keeps the reservation attached to a machine so usage and invoice still line up.
alternatives: Hard lock refuses the second hold
Overbooking pool assigns a machine at pickup

qaEntries.name: I built the reservation database. Why pay you?
qaEntries.question: I built the reservation database. Why pay you?
qaEntries.answer: The maintenance database should stay with Halverson. What is in front of Northgate is a different problem: tier pricing that resolves from the member record, overbooking expressed as a rule rather than as Tom's memory, and usage arriving as structured data before an invoice can be trusted. Each piece is manageable alone. They interact, and that is the work.
qaEntries.dependencyAsk: Which parts do you want to keep, and which do you want handed over end to end?

qaEntries.name: Two tiers and nine rates. Why is pricing hard?
qaEntries.question: Two tiers and nine rates. Why is pricing hard?
qaEntries.answer: The table is easy. Getting the right row every time is what fails today, and 41 roster entries carry no tier at all. Pricing off the member record also surfaces the disagreement in Northgate's own documents about the associate multiplier.
qaEntries.dependencyAsk: Which document governs the associate multiplier, and who can settle it this week?

qaEntries.name: We overbook on purpose. Your system will just block it.
qaEntries.question: We overbook on purpose. Your system will just block it.
qaEntries.answer: Only if it is designed badly. The recommended design keeps the overbooking and adds a conflict queue, so double holds stay legal and become visible for the first time. That queue is also the record the member dispute process needs.
qaEntries.dependencyAsk: Is reallocation seniority by join date, equity share, or Tom's judgment?

qaEntries.name: The tracker already reports hours. Isn't billing just reading that?
qaEntries.question: The tracker already reports hours. Isn't billing just reading that?
qaEntries.answer: Reading it is the easy half. Nobody has produced credentials or a test device. Then engine hours have to become billable days under a rule that does not exist yet, because a machine idling in a yard reports hours too.
qaEntries.dependencyAsk: Who holds the tracker contract, and can we get a test device before the design session?
